title: The Place Where the Earth Learned to Say No

features.name: root boundary
features.desc-on-touch: Roots have risen through soil and stopped the plow. What touches here knows the difference between refusal and obstruction.

features.name: fault line
features.desc-on-touch: Soil that will not move. The archive's first casing rests here, refusing extraction; the ground holds it as a kept thing.

features.name: utterance marks
features.desc-on-touch: Striations in stone where the earth has spoken. Each refusal left its mark. You read them as a language of no.

features.name: settling weight
features.desc-on-touch: What the earth holds settles into it. This ground knows the pressure of intention meeting resistance.

features.name: fenced boundary
features.desc-on-touch: You feel the edge where refusal meets the next field. The fence here is made of 'no'. Both sides are listening.

reverie.title: REVERIE — the field where the plow broke
narr: You stand beside her as the blade hits stone. The
engine stalls. She's laughing—it's a good laugh,
the kind that knows when the ground is right to
resist. 'It's telling us something,' she says. You
listen to the grass. The answer is no. Both of
you smile at how clearly it spoke.

inscription: the ground said no, and both the plow and the archive learned to listen
